title: The Quiet Side of the Signal

segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [quiet cabin ventilation hum] [softly] Find a position that can remain easy for a while. Let your eyes close if that feels comfortable, and imagine you are seated inside a quiet craft travelling without hurry.

[soft, slow, warm voice] Begin with the furthest sound you can detect. Perhaps traffic, wind, pipes, or a room beyond this one. Let the outer instruments receive the signal without chasing its source.

[soft, slow, warm voice] Now notice sounds closer to you... the room itself... clothing shifting... the small machinery of breathing. Nothing needs to disappear. You are simply changing which dial receives your attention.

[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice light and darkness behind the eyelids. Colours may flicker like distant panels. Allow the visual channel to dim by itself, without squeezing the eyes or pushing anything away.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice temperature where air touches the skin. Then feel the quieter information beneath it: pressure, weight, and the steady contact of the surface supporting you.

[soft, slow, warm voice] [thoughtfully] Pratyahara is not a locked door. The senses may keep sending messages. Imagine placing those messages on a gentle night mode, while attention turns toward the cabin within.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Rest with the breath as sensation rather than sound. Feel a small movement at the nostrils, chest, or belly. Choose whichever signal asks the least effort from you.
[soft, slow, warm voice] If an outer sound becomes bright again, let it arrive. There is no failed withdrawal. Notice it... allow it... then return to the quietest inner coordinate you can find.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Imagine the craft crossing a region where the stars are hidden, yet navigation continues. For a few breaths, let simple inner sensation be enough to guide you.

[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] You do not have to become empty or perfectly still. Thoughts, sounds, and feelings can remain in the background while you rest nearer to the centre of experience.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Begin turning the outer instruments up again. Include the room, the air, the sounds, and the shape of your body as one complete field.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Move your hands and feet. Let the eyes open when ready, bringing a little of the quiet side of the signal with you.
